howItWorks.dollarCostTitle: A dollar's price is the middle of real offers, every hour
howItWorks.dollarCostLead: Each country gets one price for a dollar every hour, built like this.
dollarCostPoints: A stablecoin is a coin that stays worth one US dollar.
We take the {minAds} cheapest offers to sell one on the exchange people there use. The middle offer is the price, so one odd seller cannot move it.
We set that price against the official rate at the same moment. The percentage is how much more a dollar really costs than that rate says.
A positive percentage means people pay more than the official rate. A negative one means they pay less.
With fewer than {minAds} sellers we publish no price. You see a gap, never a guess.
howItWorks.sendingCostTitle: Sending cost is the money lost against the mid-market rate
howItWorks.sendingCostLead: We price each app and the stablecoin route at {amounts} amounts, with the exchange fees and the fee for moving the coin counted. Look at the one closest to what you send.
howItWorks.sendingCostAmounts: The amounts are {amountList}, in the currency you send from.
sendingCostPoints: The mid-market rate is the middle price banks trade at with each other.
Whatever your recipient gets below that rate is what sending costs you.
howItWorks.notMeasuredTitle: Some costs are not in our figures, so check these yourself
notMeasured: The official rate updates only once a day. On days a currency moves fast, the gap we show can be a day behind.
Some exchanges do not publish what your bank charges to send money there, so we leave it out. Check your own bank's fee before you compare.
Some app prices are offers for a first transfer. If you have used that app before, you may pay more than we show.
We measure stablecoins only. If you are buying cash at a money changer, treat our numbers as a guide, not a quote.
howItWorks.sourcesTitle: Every price comes from a public source you can check
sourcesPoints: Dollar prices: Binance P2P, a marketplace where people trade with each other, {top}.
Official rates: open.er-api.com, frankfurter.app, Argentina's central bank.
App prices: {ownWord} apps quote us directly. The rest come from a public price comparison.

howItWorks.methodLede: How much you could buy at each price, the round-trip rules, and this hour's counts.
howItWorks.thresholdCounts: This hour {priced} currencies have a price and {notPriced} show a gap instead of a guess. A currency is priced when at least ten people are selling or an exchange gives a live price.
howItWorks.methodLink: See how much you could buy at each price, and the full technical rules →
howItWorks.reactionCounts: We can test this in {qualified} of {total} countries. Each has at least {hours} hours of unbroken hourly prices.
howItWorks.reactionStep: We count an official rate move once it passes {threshold}%. The street price has caught up once it closes {closed}% of the gap that move opened. We look for that for up to {days} days.
howItWorks.reactionFindingLead: We guessed that where people pay most over the official rate, prices react slowest. Across every country we can test, the two are {relation}.
howItWorks.reactionRelationWeak: barely linked, with a score of {r} where zero means no link
howItWorks.reactionFindingBody: Algeria ({ccy}) has one of the widest gaps on the site, yet its prices react among the fastest. Turkey trades close to the official rate and reacts far slower. So a wide gap does not mean slow prices. See {countriesPage} for each country's own numbers.

howItWorks.askPlaceholder: Ask how any number was made
howItWorks.askNote: The code and every data file are public.
howItWorks.askMethodTracked: Each hour we take the middle price from {evidence} ({source}). We set it against the official rate from the same check. The gap between them is the number. Nothing is estimated or smoothed.
howItWorks.askMethodGeneric: Each hour we take the middle of real offers and set it against the official rate. The gap is the number, never an estimate. With fewer than ten sellers, a country shows a reason instead. Every figure links to a file you can open.
